I take AI systems that work in a demo and make them work in production. In practice that means multi-agent architecture, tool and permission design, retrieval that stays accurate under real data, evaluation pipelines that catch regressions before users do, and fine-tuning when a smaller local model beats an API call.
We already built an agent with n8n or a no-code tool. Is that wasted?

No, and it is usually the right way to start. A prototype proves the workflow is worth building. What tends to break next is everything around it: permissions, auditability, cost at volume, and knowing whether a change made the system better or worse. That is the work I do.
Can you work with our existing team?
Yes, and it is the arrangement I prefer. I have spent most of my career embedded with in-house teams. I would rather leave your engineers able to run the system than leave them dependent on me.
Consulting through RADFAB is the main engagement model, but I am open to the right full-time role. Easiest to just ask on a call.
A short architecture review. You show me what exists, I tell you what will break first and what it would take to fix. That is often enough on its own; if it is not, we scope the build from there.
